title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter and token/event ordering in streaming output
author: Aisha Karim
description:
Motivation: Several customers and internal fuzz tests reported malformed partial-JSON events when using the SSE streaming path. Symptoms were (1) partial JSON payloads missing or mis-ordered delimiters when tokens are emitted across chunk boundaries, and (2) token/event ordering inconsistencies under concurrent multi-connection loads. This caused OpenAI-compat clients that expect deterministic token/event ordering and properly framed partial JSON objects to fail to parse.

Root cause: Two issues: a) the framing layer used a delimiter insertion heuristic that assumed token boundaries aligned with internal chunk boundaries; when that assumption failed (long tokens, quantization artifacts, or intermediate buffering on certain NICs) a delimiter could be emitted out-of-order or dropped. b) the event marshaling path allowed parallel goroutines to interleave token events for the same response when a streaming response was proxied through the compatibility layer; a race on the per-response sequence counter led to swapped token ordering.

Changes in this PR: single continuous string description of changes below. Implemented a deterministic delimiter policy that is independent of internal chunk boundaries: delimiters are attached to logical token breaks before chunking, and carry-forward state is used when tokens span chunks. Added an explicit sequence number in SSE comment metadata (non-breaking for existing clients) for debug and to enforce ordering at the compatibility layer. Converted the response writer to use a per-response ordered queue (lock-free ring backed by a single writer goroutine) to prevent interleaving between token events for the same stream. Updated the SSE framing tests to include long-token, cross-chunk, and parallel-connection fuzz cases. Added a migration in the OpenAI compatibility layer to prefer sequence-number enforcement only for clients advertising compat-mode >= 1.2 to avoid surprising legacy consumers.

Testing and verification: New unit tests for framing/delimiter placement, integration tests with the openai-compat harness exercising chunked transfer encoding, and a small stress job ran in perf-canary for 4 hours with zero parse errors. CI: flaky integration tests fixed and rerun.

Rollout plan: Canary enabled on us-west-2 for hosted API for 48 hours, monitor parse-error-rate and token-ordering-inconsistency metrics; if stable, roll to remaining regions and Dedicated clusters.

Notes: This change keeps the SSE textual format backwards-compatible; the sequence number is in a comment field so older clients ignore it. The new framing logic is intentionally conservative to avoid adding latency.

b4c5d6f: compatibility/openai: include sse-seq comment and compat-mode check
c7d8e9a: runtime/sse: reorder writer to single-writer ring to avoid interleave races
d0e1f2b: tests: add cross-chunk long-token and parallel-connection fuzz cases
e3f4a5b: perf-canary: add stress job config for sse streaming validation
review_comments: Jonah Patel: Please add a comment explaining why we new-line the seq comment as opposed to adding a custom event field. Concern is backwards compatibility with some proxies.

Aisha Karim: Reply: using an SSE comment preserves strict compatibility with existing parsers; custom event fields resulted in multiple client-side codepaths. Added comments in sse_compat.go explaining the tradeoffs.
Marina Lopez: Found a potential race when response aborts mid-chunk. Can you add a test for connection abort during cross-chunk token?
Aisha Karim: Added test to sse_compat_test.go and handled abort by draining writer ring on cancel; ensured no double-close on response writer.
Evan Chu: CI integration was flaky initially; after fixing the test harness timing the integration passed. Approving.
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming framing and partial-JSON delimiter/order issues: ensures deterministic delimiter placement across chunk boundaries, avoids token/event interleaving, adds optional sse-seq metadata for diagnostics. Backwards-compatible.
changelog_entry: Fix: SSE streaming: partial-JSON delimiter and token ordering fixes (runtime, openai-compat).
notes: Monitored after merge: zero parse errors in canary for 48 hours. Follow-up tasks: ENG-1310 to add telemetry for seq-skipped events and a small perf audit for writer_ring allocations.
